open_points.subject: scope of personal-data disclosure for direct agent-to-service access
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` reach an agent only as digest and class; the owner alone reads them.” and “no agent ever holds it” contradict “the kernel neither gives nor checks it, and its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Is the personal-data promise limited to values returned through the kernel surface, allowing a directly accessed microservice to disclose personal data to an agent, or must direct service access also preserve the digest-and-class-only rule—and, if so, who owns and enforces it?
options: Limit K-14 to the kernel surface; direct service disclosure is governed outside the kernel
Require services or the owner to enforce digest-and-class-only disclosure on direct agent access
Prohibit direct agent access to personal-data values
open_points.default_guess: Limit K-14 to the kernel surface, because the changed exclusion explicitly gives that scope and State 3 assigns disclosure enforcement only to `surface`.
